title: Troubleshooting biGBac: a practical guide
author: Erin Cutts
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.q3ydypw
materials: Assembly	Reaction	I	had	used	both	the	following	kits	successfully:	https://www.neb.com/products/e5510-gibson-assembly-cloning-kit#Product%20Information	https://www.neb.com/products/e5520-nebuilder-hifi-dna-assembly-cloning-kit#Product%20Information	You can make your own	like	Weissmann	et al, but the kits are a nice	entry-level	way	of	cloning	with	Gibson	assembly.	Although the kit recommends using 10μL of 2x assembly mix with 10μL of	DNA	mix,	I	find	5μL	of	each	works	fine.	The	first	time	you	use	the	kit,	defrost	it	slowly	on	ice,	spin	down	condensation,	make	5μL	aliquots	on	ice	and	freeze	until	required.	I	use	PCR	tubes	and	use	a	PCR	machine	for	the	assembly	reaction. Mix	on	ice.	• Vector:	(pBIG1a,	1b,	etc)	50-100ng	• Inserts:	5	fold	molar	excess	for	inserts	smaller	than	the	vector	and	a	2	fold	excess	for	inserts	of	similar	of	larger	size	(4kb	or	bigger).	• Water	to	5μL	Add	this	to	a	5μL	aliquot	of	2x	assembly	mix. • Incubate	at	50°C	for	15-60	minutes.	(15	minutes	is	fine	for	two	fragment	assembly,	but	more	fragments	require	longer). • Transform	2μL	of	assembly	into	20μL	of	cells	that	come	with	the	kit	(any	highly competent cells for cloning purposes should be fine), plate	onto	amp+spec	LB	plates	and	grow	over	night	at	37°C.	I	like	to	do	a	control	using	an	equivalent	amount	of	vector	without	assembly	mix	to	give	an	idea	of	how	many	background	colonies	there	may	be.	For	the	first	assembly	reaction	you	ever do, you could also use the assembly control provided with the Gibson	assembly	kit	to	ensure	your	assembly	mix	works	as	expected. Screening	by	colony	PCR	Hopefully	your	transformation	plates	have	~30	or	more	colonies.	I’ve designed a set of 4 primers	( S 1 A-D)	f o r s c r e e n i n g with colony PCR	whether	assembly	has	occurred.	When	all	primers	are	used	for	a	PCR	reaction,	this results	i n t h r e e p r o d u c t s i f a ssembly has been successful, but only one of	size	350bp	if	no	insert	has	assembled	(figure	4).	Partial	assemblies	are	possible,	so all three bands need to be present. I find screening at least 5 colonies of	assembly	reaction	is	advisable,	if	you	assemble	more	than	3	genes,	or	the	genes	are variable sizes, I would recommend you screen as many as practical (using	strip	PCR	tubes	or	plates	means	this	can	be	high	through-put). I	use	the	KAPPA	robust	PCR	kit,	because	it	always	work	for	me:	https://www.n-genetics.com/file/KAPA2G_Robust_TDS_KR0379_v7.16.pdf • Leave	transformation	plates	until	colonies	are	a	reasonable	size.

steps.title: Design Constructs
steps.instruction: Plan the assembly of gene expression cassettes (GECs) into pBIG1 and pBIG2 vectors using APE (A Plasmid Editor).

substeps.instruction: Group stable sub-complexes into individual pBIG1 vectors, limiting each to 3-4 genes.
Perform computational digests with SwaI and PacI to ensure predicted band patterns are unique and do not overlap in size.
Ensure all constructs lack PmeI, SwaI, and PacI restriction sites within the genes or downstream cloning regions.

steps.title: Amplify pLIB Expression Cassettes
steps.instruction: PCR amplify each pLIB GEC using Cas primers to add Gibson assembly overlaps (α, β, γ, δ, ε, ω).

substeps.instruction: Use CasI_for/rev for the first gene, CasII_for/rev for the second, and Casω_rev (with the forward version of the second-to-last reverse primer) for the final gene.
Prepare PCR mix: 100-200ng pLIB DNA template, 0.5μL Phusion 5x buffer, 1μL dNTPs (10mM), 2.5μL Forward primer (10μM), 2.5μL Reverse primer (10μM), 1μL Phusion polymerase, and water up to 50μL.
Run Phusion cycle: annealing temperature 65°C, extension time 15-30s per kb of the longest gene, for 30-35 cycles.
Perform gel extraction. If sub-cloning with Gibson assembly, add 1μL DpnI and incubate at 37°C for 1 hour prior to gel extraction to remove plasmid template.

steps.title: Linearize pBIG1 Vector
steps.instruction: Digest the pBIG1 vector with SwaI to create blunt ends with α and β overlap regions.

substeps.instruction: Prepare digest mix: 10μg Mini prep DNA, 20-30μL 10x buffer 3.1, 4μL SwaI enzyme, 1-2μL water, up to 40μL.
Incubate overnight at room temperature.
Add an additional 1μL of SwaI enzyme and incubate for one more hour.
Inactivate the enzyme at 65°C for 20 minutes.
Gel-extract the vector in a 1% agarose gel using the Zymo gel extraction kit (elute in 10μL water). If the fragment is >8kb, add an equal volume of water to the gel volume to improve yield.
Quantify DNA concentration using Nanodrop.

steps.title: Assemble and Screen pBIG1 Constructs
steps.instruction: Perform Gibson assembly of the linearized pBIG1 vector and PCR products, then screen colonies.

substeps.instruction: Perform Gibson assembly and plate on appropriate antibiotic media.
Screen colonies via PCR: pick colonies into 80μL sterile water (avoid agar).

Prepare colony PCR mix: 0.2μL 10x dNTPs (10mM), 0.5μL primer mix (10μM each of S1A-D), 2μL 5x Buffer B, 0.1μL Kappa robust enzyme, 1μL water, and 1μL colony water (total volume 62μL, aliquot 9μL per tube).
Run PCR: annealing temperature 58°C, extension time 30s, for 30-35 cycles.
Analyze on a 2% agarose gel; correct assemblies should show three bands (230 bp, 380 bp, and 458 bp), while empty vectors show one band (~350 bp).
Pick 3-4 colonies with the correct three-band pattern for overnight culture and mini-prep.

steps.title: Verify pBIG1 Assembly
steps.instruction: Perform a diagnostic SwaI digest to confirm the presence of all assembled genes.

substeps.instruction: Prepare digest: Mini prep DNA, 1μL 10x buffer, 4.5μL water, 0.5μL SwaI.
Incubate for a few hours at room temperature and run on a 1% gel.
Verify that a DNA band exists for each gene (gene size + ~500bp).

steps.title: Assemble pBIG2 Constructs
steps.instruction: Assemble multiple pBIG1 fragments into a pBIG2 vector using PmeI digestion and Gibson assembly.

substeps.instruction: Digest pBIG1 and pBIG2 vectors with PmeI: 5-10μg Mini prep, 20-30μL 10x CutSmart buffer, 4μL PmeI enzyme, 1-2μL water, up to 50μL.
Incubate pBIG1 vectors at 37°C for a few hours; incubate pBIG2 vectors overnight.
Run 1% gel to verify band size, then gel-extract using Zymo kit (elute in 10μL water).
Perform Gibson assembly and plate on Amp+Cam plates.
Screen colonies using colony PCR with primers S2A-D (correct assembly: 424, 322, and 680 bp; empty: 800 bp).
Perform diagnostic digest on mini-preps using PacI (to check fragments) and SwaI (to check GECs) separately.

steps.title: Express in Insect Cells
steps.instruction: Transform the final constructs into insect cell systems for protein production.

substeps.instruction: Transform pLIB, pBIG1, or pBIG2 constructs into DH10emBacY cells and purify the bacmid.
Transfect the bacmid into Sf9 cells to create a P1 virus stock.
After 3 days, amplify the virus by adding transfection supernatant to create a P2 virus stock for expression.
Note: For constructs >20kb, P2 amplification may take longer.
